content: The provided text is a detailed list of drug interactions involving sulfadiazine and various other medications. 1. Sulfadiazine and Dalteparin: Sulfadiazine enhances the effects of dalteparin by competing for plasma protein binding. This interaction necessitates either avoiding the combination or using an alternative drug. Close monitoring is advised. 2. Sulfadiazine and Dapsone (Topical): Sulfadiazine increases the toxicity of topical dapsone by reducing its metabolism. This combination may induce methemoglobinemia. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 3. Sulfadiazine and Diclofenac: Sulfadiazine elevates diclofenac levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution is advised, and the diclofenac dose should not exceed 50 mg twice daily. 4. Sulfadiazine and Diflunisal: Diflunisal increases sulfadiazine levels through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 5. Sulfadiazine and Digoxin: Sulfadiazine raises digoxin levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both drugs. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 6. Sulfadiazine and Dronabinol: Sulfadiazine increases dronabinol levels or effects by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Dronabinol is a CYP2C9 substrate. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Sulfadiazine and Drospirenone: Drospirenone increases sulfadiazine levels through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 8. Sulfadiazine and Eluxadoline: Sulfadiazine increases eluxadoline levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Due to incomplete information on eluxadoline metabolism, caution is advised when coadministered with strong CYP2C9/10 inhibitors. Close monitoring is necessary. 9. Sulfadiazine and Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF: This combination decreases sulfadiazine levels by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Elvitegravir is a moderate CYP2C9 inducer. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 10. Sulfadiazine and Enoxaparin: Sulfadiazine enhances the effects of enoxaparin by reducing its metabolism and competing for plasma protein binding. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 11. Sulfadiazine and Erdafitinib: Sulfadiazine increases erdafitinib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for adverse reactions and consider dose adjustments. 12. Sulfadiazine and Estradiol: Sulfadiazine decreases estradiol levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 13. Sulfadiazine and Conjugated Estrogens: Sulfadiazine reduces the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Sulfadiazine and Ethinyl Estradiol: Sulfadiazine decreases ethinyl estradiol levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Sulfadiazine and Insulin (Various Types): Sulfadiazine enhances the effects of various insulin formulations (e.g., insulin aspart, insulin glargine, insulin lispro) through unspecified mechanisms. Concomitant use may require insulin dosage adjustments and increased glucose monitoring. Close monitoring is essential. 16. Sulfadiazine and Methotrexate: Sulfadiazine increases methotrexate toxicity by competing for plasma protein binding. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Close monitoring is necessary. 17. Sulfadiazine and Methoxsalen: This combination increases the phototoxicity of both drugs due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Sulfadiazine and Microbiota Oral: Sulfadiazine reduces the efficacy of microbiota oral products by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration. Complete antibiotic regimens 2–4 days before initiating microbiota oral therapy. 19. Sulfadiazine and Pyrimethamine: This combination increases bone marrow toxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Close monitoring is recommended. 20. Sulfadiazine and Probenecid: Probenecid increases sulfadiazine levels through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is advised. 21. Sulfadiazine and Promazine: Promazine increases sulfadiazine toxicity through an unspecified mechanism, leading to enhanced myelosuppression. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Sulfadiazine and Protamine: Sulfadiazine enhances the effects of protamine by reducing its metabolism and competing for plasma protein binding. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 23. Sulfadiazine and Pyridoxine: Sulfadiazine decreases pyridoxine levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 24. Sulfadiazine and Pretomanid: This combination increases the risk of hepatotoxicity. Avoid coadministration with hepatotoxic agents, including alcohol and herbal supplements. Use alternative drugs if possible. 25. Sulfadiazine and Rucaparib: Rucaparib increases sulfadiazine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely.
